tier_reason: Peer-reviewed USENIX ATC'17 paper compares HC Redis against default Redis. Fig. 11 (NodeJS, Dynamic Intro, 5k objects) shows 10.0 vs 11.3 kreq/s, miss rate 0.33 vs 0.27, +11.6%; Fig. 7 (Django-Wiki) shows 21.1 vs 23.7 req/s (+12.3%). The CPU (Xeon E5620) is stated and the runner code is public, but no compiler or flags are given, so it is not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Hyperbolic caching improves end-to-end application throughput by ~5-10% over default Redis (abstract) and lowers miss rates by 10-37% on the NodeJS synthetic workloads, with throughput up to ~14% higher. Example, Fig. 11 (NodeJS over Redis, Dynamic Intro, 5k-object cache): 10.0 vs 11.3 kreq/s and miss rate 0.33 vs 0.27 for default vs HC Redis (+11.6%). Fig. 7 (Django-Wiki, Wikipedia Jan 2008 trace): 21.1 vs 23.7 req/s (+12.3%) for default vs HC.
corrections.caveats: This repo is archived. It holds the Python simulator plus the NodeJS and Django benchmark runners (GitHub language: Python), not the Redis patch itself. The paper's 380-line C Redis change (forked at Redis 3.0) lives in a separate repo, github.com/kantai/redis-hyperbolic-caching (BSD-3-Clause, archived, 6 stars, last commit 2017-05-18). Default Redis eviction here means Redis's sampled approximate LRU. The 2021-12-09 date is the archive push, not a commit.

notes: The claim numbers match the paper; 10.0 vs 11.3 is kreq/s on the page, so 'req/ms' was numerically equivalent but not the page's unit. Last commit on the default branch is 2017-07-14, and the repo is not a GitHub fork. The record's language 'C' fits only the separate Redis-prototype repo, since this repo is Python. That field is not correctable here.

tier_reason: The peer-reviewed NSDI'18 paper's abstract states LHD needs on average 8x less space than LRU and 2-3x less than recent policies, and that RankCache at 16 threads improves throughput 8x over LRU and 2x over CLOCK. The repo has only the simulator, and the paper gives no CPU model, compiler or flags, so it is not A.

corrections.license: MIT (verbatim MIT text, Copyright 2017-2018 Carnegie Mellon University, plus a non-binding request to cite the LHD paper; GitHub reports NOASSERTION)
corrections.caveats: The 8x/2x throughput numbers are for RankCache, a separate prototype built on memcached 1.4.33 that is not in this repo. Its own README calls the CMU-CORGI/LHD repo 'simulation code' only, so the throughput claim cannot be reproduced from it. The throughput test ran inside one server with the network bypassed, on a random Zipfian trace with same-size objects. The paper's intro gives a different figure (16x over list-based LRU; 2x over CLOCK at a 90% hit ratio) than the abstract's 8x. The 8x space saving is an average across the Memcachier and MSR traces. MIT license: no patent grant.

notes: The claim is quoted almost verbatim from the abstract. The metadata (25 stars, last commit 2018-07-23, abandoned, not a fork) checks out. The LICENSE file is standard MIT plus a citation request, so 'copyable' stands.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed NSDI'20 paper. The simulations compare LRB against B-LRU, LRU, LFUDA, TinyLFU, LeCaR and others, and the prototype is compared with unmodified ATS. Code is public (webcachesim2 plus lrb-prototype), but only the VM type is given (no CPU model, compiler or flags), so it is not A. Tier stays B; the verdict is a downgrade because the claim misattributes the 44% win to an LRU baseline.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Simulations on 6 production CDN traces: LRB reduces WAN traffic by 4-25% vs B-LRU (the LRU-with-Bloom-filter-admission production CDN design), and by over 13% on average across cache sizes. It is robust across traces where LRU4, LFUDA, TinyLFU and LeCaR each win only on some. Prototype, Wikipedia trace, 1TB flash cache, days 12-14: LRB cuts average WAN bandwidth by 44% and p95 bandwidth by 43% vs unmodified Apache Traffic Server 8.0.3, which the paper says approximates FIFO eviction, not LRU.
corrections.workload: Simulation (webcachesim2) replaying 6 production CDN traces (Wikipedia 14-day plus 5 from two other CDNs) at a range of cache sizes vs B-LRU, LRU, LRU4, LFUDA, TinyLFU, LeCaR and others. Also a CDN flash-cache prototype built on Apache Traffic Server 8.0.3, replaying the Wikipedia trace with a 1TB cache.
corrections.caveats: The paper's prototype baseline, unmodified ATS, approximates FIFO eviction, not LRU. Against LRU-family baselines the win is the simulated 4-25% WAN-traffic reduction vs B-LRU. Raw throughput is essentially tied (LRB 11.72 vs ATS 11.66 Gbps), and LRB uses more peak CPU (16% vs 9%); the win is in bandwidth and miss ratio. The CPU model and compiler/flags are not stated. The repo is a GitHub fork of dasebe/webcachesim; the ATS prototype is in a separate repo, sunnyszy/lrb-prototype (Apache-2.0).

notes: The 44%/43% and 11.72/11.66 Gbps numbers are on the page, but the record wrongly calls ATS LRU-based (the paper says it approximates FIFO). The default branch's last commit is 2023-01-20; 2023-12-18 is only pushed_at. That is more than 3 years ago, so the repo is abandoned. is_fork_of is set to dasebe/webcachesim.
